title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics of 'analysis situs' (second draft). The setting has the following ingredients.
- A set L of 'lieux' (places, points).
- A set M of 'multistructures' or figures X. In the set-theoretic models M ⊂ Figel(L); a figure is roughly a family of subsets of L.
- An 'ombre' (shadow) omb(X) ⊂ L, the support of a figure.
- A refinement order X' ≪ X.
- A primitive symmetric relation on M, written with a crossed sign under which M is placed. Page 60 uses it to define a disjointness relation X ∥ Y on figures.

Page 60 showed that set-theoretic 'disposition' does not imply geometric 'disposition'. It then formulated (*): if X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y and X ∥ Y, then X' ∥ Y'. In words, disjointness is inherited by refinements.

Page 61 opens by declining to make (*) an axiom. Grothendieck sees it as a special case of a much more general 'axiome de raccordement (recollement) des raffinements', to be stated later. That axiom does not refer to places. He then announces two axioms that do involve places.

(1) At 9, marginal title 'Critère de disjonction par les lieux'. Let X, Y ∈ M. Suppose every place x ∈ omb(X) and every place y ∈ omb(Y) are disjoint, x ∥ y. Then X ∥ Y. This is a local-to-global principle: disjointness of figures is detected pointwise on their shadows.

(2) For 'set-theoretic' (and hence 'geo-set-theoretic') situations he adds Atens 2: distinct places x ≠ y in L stand in the primitive separation relation of M. Inside M ⊂ Figel(L) this becomes Atens* 4: for x ≠ y the singleton figures {{x}} and {{y}} are M-separated.

Where this leads (page 62). The corollary there combines At 9 and Atens 2 with the heredity (*). It gives: F ∥ G if and only if all pairs of their places are disjoint. In set-theoretic models, assuming no point is disjoint from itself, this amounts to omb(F) ∩ omb(G) = ∅. Disjointness of figures is thereby reduced to disjointness of shadows. Page 62 then states the companion axiom At 9′ for transversality (⋔): shadows meeting exactly in the shadow of the intersection.

Purpose. The page serves the foundational project of an axiomatic, point-and-figure 'géométrie de position'. It aims to relate the abstract separation and disjointness relations on figures to the underlying point set.
errors: No outright error. There is a small logical dependency: the 'il faut' (necessity) half of the page-62 corollary needs heredity of disjointness to points, i.e. (*) or the later refinement-gluing axiom. Grothendieck explicitly refrains from adopting that axiom on this page. The equivalence is therefore conditional on an axiom still to come.
The reduction 'F ∥ G iff omb(F) ∩ omb(G) = ∅' also tacitly requires that no point is disjoint from itself (x ∥ x false). This is not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Heredity of disjointness under refinement, viewed as a special case of a general 'recollement des raffinements' axiom
ideas.modern_name: Monotonicity of a disjointness/apartness relation; a gluing (sheaf-like) condition for refinements

ideas.what: At 9: figures are disjoint if all their points (elements of their shadows) are pairwise disjoint
ideas.modern_name: Point-detection / local-to-global criterion for disjointness; akin to 'atomicity' axioms in mereotopology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; mereotopology (Whitehead, Tarski, Clarke), point-free topology

ideas.what: Atens 2 / Atens* 4: in set-theoretic models, distinct points (singleton figures {{x}}) are separated
ideas.modern_name: T1/separation-of-points-type axiom; discreteness of points under apartness

missed.claim: Grothendieck's axiomatics of figures, shadows, disjointness and refinement in 'Analysis situs' is a region-plus-points geometry closely parallel to mereotopology and contact algebras (Whitehead, de Laguna, Tarski, Clarke, later Düntsch–Vakarelov). Here, disjointness of figures is checked through their points. To my knowledge no comparison between these 1986 notes and that literature has been made.
missed.quote: Critère de disjonction par les lieux ... ∀ x ∈ omb(X), y ∈ omb(Y), x et y soient disjoints ... Alors X ∥ Y
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This would place Grothendieck's late foundational 'géométrie de position' within an existing research area (qualitative spatial reasoning, point-free topology). It might suggest that his axioms correspond to known representation theorems.

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces but does not state here a general 'axiome de raccordement des raffinements', which would subsume heredity of disjointness. Whether and how it is formulated later in the manuscript (pages 72ff.?) is an open thread for readers of the archive.
missed.quote: un cas particulier d'un axiome de raccordement des raffinements, beaucoup plus général, dont il sera question plus bas
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This minor thread matters mainly for reconstructing the full axiom system.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary foundational axioms: pointwise criteria for disjointness and separation of distinct points. They are part of an unpublished axiomatic project. They are mathematically routine, though historically interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's late 'analysis situs' program.
transcription_corrections: 'Comp(X)', 'Comp(Y)' should read 'omb(X)', 'omb(Y)' (ombre = shadow), consistent with page 62.
Line 2-3: 'ou je le vois comme un particulier' should read 'car je le vois comme cas particulier'.
'axiome de raccordement des raffinements' is possibly 'recollement'.
'j'ai envie de [?] deux axiomes' is likely 'j'ai envie de formuler deux axiomes' (or 'de donner').
'pour une catégorie ensembliste' is likely 'pour une situation/structure ensembliste'. 'géoniensembliste' is likely 'géomensembliste'.

The relation symbol in Atens 2 / Atens* 4 (rendered \between) appears to be the same crossed symbol with M below that is used on page 60 (rendered \not\leq there), i.e. the primitive separation relation of M, not 'between'.
'Alors X et Y le sont X ∥ Y' should read 'Alors X et Y sont disjoints : X ∥ Y'.
